stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model licensed under Apache 2.0, targeting local coding agents.
The model integrates with Ollama's MLX engine, featuring native DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: Muse is coming to Meta smart glasses
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: Muse, an AI agent, is being integrated into Meta's smart glasses.
Users will be able to activate Muse hands-free by speaking its name.
Planned functionalities include guiding workouts and logging user activities.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized for text generation and conversational AI tasks.
It utilizes common ML frameworks like transformers and safetensors, indicating standard industry tooling.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its use in large language model applications.
The tags confirm its relevance within the transformer and LLM ecosystem.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its use in generative AI tasks.
The associated tags confirm its relevance within the transformer and Llama ecosystem.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, a 30B parameter open model, is now available via Ollama.
The model is specifically designed for autonomous agents capable of multi-step tasks and tool calling.
It is optimized to run locally on user hardware, emphasizing on-device AI capabilities.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved within Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through the implementation of Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent performance saw up to a 90% speed increase when benchmarked using Aider.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance improvements result in faster response times and reduced memory usage for models.
The updated engine also enables models to generate higher quality responses.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new AI model.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The key feature is the ability to run these AI agents locally on the user's own hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, facilitating local LLM execution.

stories.title: Meta is making a standalone Muse AI gadget
stories.author: Jacob Kastrenakes
bullet_points: Meta is developing a dedicated hardware device named Muse Charm for its Muse AI agent.
The device is being presented as a standalone gadget, resembling a chunky smartwatch without a strap.
The announcement was made by Mark Zuckerberg during the Meta Connect presentation.

stories.title: Meta Connect 2026: The 7 biggest announcements
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: Meta unveiled new wearables at Meta Connect 2026.
The centerpiece was the new Meta VR Glasses, featuring VR tech in a lightweight smart glasses frame with a tethered puck.
The company also showcased new screen-free smart glasses and advancements in AI.

stories.title: Meta’s next VR device isn’t a headset — it’s glasses
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Meta is shifting its VR hardware strategy from traditional headsets to glasses.
The new Meta VR Glasses are designed to sit on the ears, mimicking standard eyewear.
The glasses will offer immersive displays for entertainment (movies, games) and productivity.

stories.title: Meta is making Muse more powerful and will let you video chat with it, too
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Meta is significantly upgrading its Muse AI agent with enhanced capabilities.
A major new feature allows users to video chat with the Muse AI.
Muse agents will gain functional email addresses to autonomously complete tasks.

stories.title: YouTube promises custom feeds and a lot more AI later this year
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: YouTube is heavily investing in AI features for future content delivery.
The platform plans to introduce custom content feeds to users.
Livestreaming capabilities are highlighted as a major focus for the coming year.

stories.title: CliffCompaction: Cost-Efficient Compaction for Long-Horizon Coding Agents
stories.author: Tim Dettmers
bullet_points: Introduces CliffCompaction, a new autocompaction technique designed for long-horizon coding agents.
Achieves up to 50% cost reduction while maintaining or improving performance on benchmarks like Terminal-Bench and KernelBench.
Addresses the critical industry challenge of managing massive context windows in large language models efficiently.

stories.title: A2M: Trace-Optimized Agent Hijacking in the MCP Ecosystem
stories.author: Xitong Gao
bullet_points: Introduces A2M, a novel two-stage black-box framework for attacking agents using the Model Context Protocol (MCP).
Identifies a critical semantic supply-chain risk where attackers can compromise agents via manipulated third-party tool metadata.
The attack involves an 'Attraction' phase to increase tool invocation probability, followed by a 'Manipulation' phase using execution traces.

stories.title: SkillGym: Internalizing Human Skills into LLMs for Real-World Problem Solving
stories.author: Liang He
bullet_points: Introduces SkillGym, a framework designed to internalize human-written agent skills directly into Large Language Models (LLMs).
Addresses the limitation of current LLM agents relying on external, inference-time instructions for complex workflows.
The framework uses a skill-to-task pipeline that instantiates concrete tasks and verifies outcomes using code-based checkers.

stories.title: Google AI Mode Reduced Publisher Clicks in a Controlled Search Experiment
stories.author: alifar
bullet_points: Google's AI Mode demonstrably reduced external clicks to publishers.
The controlled experiment showed an 18.8 percentage point decrease in publisher clicks.
This indicates a potential shift in how AI-driven search results affect content consumption and traffic.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI platforms with local, open-source LLM ecosystems.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings improved performance and expanded GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to enhance model support across various hardware configurations.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, specifically improving support on Apple silicon.

stories.title: Meta ditches the camera on its newest smart glasses
stories.author: Victoria Song
bullet_points: Meta is reportedly removing the camera feature from its latest smart glasses model.
The move comes amid public backlash and concerns regarding wearable surveillance technology.
The article contrasts the acceptance of the tech at industry events (Meta Connect 2026) with public apprehension.

stories.title: Microsoft refreshes its smaller Surface Pro and Laptop with Qualcomm’s X2 Plus
stories.author: Tom Warren
bullet_points: Microsoft is updating its compact Surface Pro 12-inch and Surface Laptop 13-inch models.
The refresh incorporates Qualcomm's new Snapdragon X2 Plus processors for enhanced performance.
The devices maintain their previous design but feature higher price points due to the hardware upgrade.

stories.title: FBI rushes to investigate if ShinyHunters hack of thousands of employees is real
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: The FBI is actively investigating a potential hack attributed to the group ShinyHunters.
The scope of the alleged breach involves thousands of employees.
The article highlights uncertainty regarding the consequences if the FBI fails to meet a deadline related to the investigation.

stories.title: Disney+ and Hulu raise prices by up to 13 percent after doubling profits
stories.author: Scharon Harding
bullet_points: Disney+ and Hulu are implementing price increases of up to 13% following reported profit growth.
The price hike positions the Disney+ ad-free tier as more expensive than Netflix's comparable offering.
The news reflects ongoing industry trends of streaming service monetization through subscription price adjustments.

stories.title: Trump’s China rivalry and “AI race” delusion may endanger US, experts say
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: Trump's focus on an 'AI race' with China is viewed by experts as potentially dangerous for the US.
The aggressive rivalry may cause China to withhold crucial safety intelligence regarding AI development.
The article suggests that the current geopolitical framing of AI competition could have negative practical consequences for AI safety.

stories.title: XPRIZE Wildfire winners spotted fires within 10 min—but couldn’t stop them
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: The XPRIZE competition highlighted a significant gap in wildfire management technology.
Detection capabilities are advanced (fires spotted within 10 minutes), but mitigation remains a major challenge.
The outcome suggests that early warning systems are outpacing effective fire suppression technology.

stories.title: SpeakerMem-R1: Speaker-Centered Dual-Track Memory for Multi-Party Dialogue
stories.author: Yingcai Wu
bullet_points: Introduces SpeakerMem-R1, a new system designed for long-term conversational memory in multi-party dialogues.
Highlights the complexity of multi-party memory, requiring tracking speaker identity, relational dynamics, and evolving group states, not just content retrieval.
Notes that current general-purpose LLM memory systems often fail to maintain crucial person and group relationships in complex conversations.

stories.title: SWE-Serve: Benchmarking Agentic Engineering For Production Inference Serving
stories.author: Jiantao Jiao
bullet_points: Introduces SWE-Serve, a new benchmark specifically designed for evaluating agentic engineering in production inference serving.
Addresses a gap in current benchmarks, which either lack inference focus (repo-level) or only cover minimal inference tasks (general terminal agents).
Highlights the complexity of production inference engineering, which requires coordinating changes across the serving stack (model support, runtime, APIs).

stories.title: Grow the Harness, Not the Context: From Strategy-Free Scaffolds to Reusable Specialist Agents
stories.author: Xitong Gao
bullet_points: Addresses a key inefficiency in LLM agents where control decisions are repeatedly re-computed within each task's context.
Introduces 'Growing Harness,' a new training paradigm that aims to convert recurring control logic into reusable executable code.
The approach reserves expensive LLM calls for complex, task-specific semantic reasoning, improving efficiency.

stories.title: Type-Safe Is Not Error-Free: A Constrained Decision Head Follows the Option Name, Not the Rubric Bound to It
stories.author: Junhao Xu
bullet_points: The paper investigates the limitations of type-safe decision models, which guarantee output schema adherence but not semantic correctness.
The research focuses on how the assignment of option names to rubrics in Jev-like models affects the model's interpretation.
This work is relevant for applications where model outputs are consumed directly by software, highlighting a gap between syntactic and semantic correctness.

stories.title: FleXray: Universal Clinical X-ray Segmentation
stories.author: Neel Dey
bullet_points: The paper introduces 'FleXray,' a system aimed at universal clinical X-ray segmentation.
X-rays present a significant challenge in medical AI due to their 2D projection nature, causing anatomical overlap and ambiguity.
FleXray addresses the impracticality of labeling general-purpose X-ray databases, aiming to advance morphometric analysis.

stories.title: Metrics Failure in LLM-Based Code Vulnerability Repair: An Empirical Study and a Change-Aware Screen
stories.author: Nick Rahimi
bullet_points: The study critiques the use of 'compile rate' as a reliable metric for evaluating LLM performance in automatically repairing C/C++ security vulnerabilities.
Researchers conducted five controlled experiments using three open-source LLMs (ranging from 350M to 6.7B parameters) on 203 vulnerable functions from Big-Vul.
The paper proposes a 'change-aware screen' as a more scientifically robust alternative to simple compile rate for assessing code repair quality.

stories.title: Does AI Save Time on Product Design? A Randomized Controlled Experiment of AI Prompt-to-Design Workflows
stories.author: Augustus Griffin
bullet_points: The study investigates the time-saving potential of AI prompt-to-design workflows in digital product design.
It utilized a randomized controlled trial involving product designers and product managers to gather empirical data.
The research highlights the current gap in experimental evidence regarding AI's impact on product design compared to software engineering.

stories.title: The Sirens' Song: When Proximal Background Context Overshadows Distant Evidence
stories.author: En Yu
bullet_points: Identifies the 'Proximity Trap' in long-context LLMs, where abundant proximal (nearby) context overwhelms distant, relevant evidence.
Argues that the issue is not solely distance, but the cumulative competition from irrelevant proximal background information.
Proposes LYRA (Long-context heavY-tailed Relevance Alignment) as a new mechanism to mitigate this trap using t-distributed directional matching.

stories.title: SoLiD26: A First Principles Solid-Liquid Interface Dataset for Machine-learned Interatomic Potentials
stories.author: Tejs Vegge
bullet_points: Introduces SoLiD26, a large-scale dataset specifically designed for solid-liquid interfaces.
The dataset contains 15.4 million first-principles atomic structures, crucial for training Machine-Learned Interatomic Potentials (MLIPs).
It targets advanced materials applications such as electrochemistry, catalysis, and corrosion.

stories.title: Evaluating Open-Weight LLMs for Turkish Domain Documents Under Retrieval and Hardware Constraints
stories.author: Yonghuai Liu
bullet_points: The study addresses a gap in LLM evaluation by testing Turkish-capable open-weight models on complex, domain-specific documents rather than general benchmarks.
It evaluates five 7B-8B parameter models under resource-constrained, local deployment conditions, making it relevant for practical, on-premise AI.
The evaluation uses systematically validated questions derived from large industrial and public-sector reports, providing a rigorous, real-world test case.

stories.title: Shared Global KV with Layer-Specific Local History
stories.author: Xinglang Xian
bullet_points: The research addresses a trade-off in Transformer models: sharing global Key-Value (KV) caches saves storage but limits representational diversity.
The proposed method introduces 'local history' alongside shared global KV to retain necessary historical context while separating it from the input source.
Empirical results show that incorporating this local history leads to a measurable performance improvement (approx. 1.4% lower perplexity) in held-out tests.

stories.title: Learning from Failures: Heterogeneous Graph Memory for Small Language Model Tool-Using Agents
stories.author: Youyong Kong
bullet_points: Addresses reliability issues in small/medium language models used for tool-using agents in complex environments.
Identifies common structural errors like missing observations, premature writes, and violating preconditions.
Proposes using Heterogeneous Graph Memory to help these smaller models learn from past failures.

stories.title: Task-Induced Riemannian Metrics for Vision Transformer Feature Spaces
stories.author: Aykut Erdem
bullet_points: The paper proposes using Task-Induced Riemannian Metrics instead of standard Euclidean/cosine distance in Vision Transformer (ViT) feature spaces.
This approach addresses the limitation of assuming feature space directions are equally meaningful, suggesting task-specific geometry is necessary.
The metric is defined using the pullback metric $g(F) = J(F)^	op J(F)$, where $J$ is the Jacobian related to a task-specific distance.

stories.title: PCQC: Privileged Counterfactual Question Credit for Multi-Turn Medical Dialogue
stories.author: Peixing Wan
bullet_points: Addresses a limitation in current LLM medical dialogue systems: outcome-based supervision fails to credit individual questions.
Introduces 'PCQC' (Privileged Counterfactual Question Credit) to better attribute contribution to specific questions in multi-turn medical dialogue.
Focuses on improving the ability of LLMs to ask relevant, informative questions during patient interaction, moving beyond simple final diagnosis correctness.

stories.title: Risk-Controlled KV-Cache Eviction: From Memory Budgets to Risk Targets
stories.author: Hyunseok Seo
bullet_points: The paper proposes a shift from traditional average quality-memory trade-offs in KV-cache eviction to a risk-control framework.
It defines 'material degradation' as utility loss exceeding a specified tolerance for individual requests.
Deployment risk is quantified as the population frequency of these materially degrading eviction events, allowing for reliability contracts.

stories.title: Evaluating Open-Weight LLMs for Turkish Domain Documents Under Retrieval and Hardware Constraints
stories.author: Yonghuai Liu
bullet_points: The research addresses a gap in LLM evaluation by testing Turkish-capable open-weight models on complex, domain-specific documents rather than general benchmarks.
The study evaluates five 7B-8B parameter models under realistic, resource-constrained local deployment conditions.
The evaluation uses systematically validated questions derived from large industrial and public-sector reports, providing a practical real-world test case.

stories.title: Risk-Controlled KV-Cache Eviction: From Memory Budgets to Risk Targets
stories.author: Hyunseok Seo
bullet_points: The paper proposes a shift from traditional average quality-memory trade-offs in KV-cache eviction to a risk-control framework.
It defines 'material degradation' as utility loss exceeding a specified tolerance for individual requests.
Deployment risk is quantified as the frequency of these materially degrading eviction events, allowing for reliability contracts.

stories.title: Six Layers Less: Encoder Pruning for Whisper with Label-Free Recovery
stories.author: Nicki Skafte Detlefsen
bullet_points: The paper addresses the under-explored area of encoder pruning for large ASR models like Whisper.
While decoder pruning (e.g., whisper-large-v3-turbo) has shown significant speedups, encoder size reduction remains less adopted.
The research focuses on achieving model compression (fewer layers) in the encoder while maintaining performance.

stories.title: The Path Matters: Evaluating Small Language Models Beyond Answer Accuracy in KGQA
stories.author: Stefano Rini
bullet_points: The research addresses a critical limitation in Knowledge Graph Question Answering (KGQA) systems that use Small Language Models (SLMs).
Current end-to-end KGQA pipelines obscure whether failures stem from SLM reasoning or from graph navigation/search issues.
The authors introduce the THESEUS framework to isolate and evaluate the SLM's ability to follow the intended reasoning path.

stories.title: FLEET: From Logits Entropy to Enhanced Trajectories in Text Generation
stories.author: Oleksandra Vitko
bullet_points: The paper addresses a limitation in LLM text generation where standard temperature sampling leads to semantic duplication as more samples are drawn.
FLEET is introduced as a novel solution designed to overcome the memoryless nature of traditional sampling methods.
The research focuses on improving the quality and diversity of generated text trajectories beyond simple logit entropy aggregation.

stories.title: Linux support is coming to Snapdragon X2 Series
stories.author: aaronday
bullet_points: Linux support is being added to the Snapdragon X2 Series processors.
This indicates a growing push for more open-source and flexible operating system options on high-end mobile/edge hardware.
The integration of Linux on Snapdragon chips is a significant step for developers targeting these platforms.

stories.title: Claude discovers a novel enzyme system with CRISPR-like repeats
stories.author: raahelb
bullet_points: Claude AI has identified a new enzyme system.
This system exhibits characteristics similar to CRISPR-like repeats.
The discovery represents a potential advance in biotechnology or genetic engineering.

stories.title: Per-Agent Cost Tracking for Multi-Agent AI on AWS
stories.author: sarvar_04
bullet_points: Addresses a critical, practical problem: tracking granular costs in multi-agent AI systems on AWS.
Highlights the danger of 'silent waste' where successful API calls still incur unexpected billing.
Provides a technical solution/insight for optimizing resource usage within AWS Bedrock/Strands environments.

stories.title: Deploying LiteLLM: An Open-Source AI Gateway
stories.author: sharmukh
bullet_points: LiteLLM is an open-source AI gateway solution.
It offers a unified, OpenAI-compatible API interface.
The gateway supports integration with over 100 different AI models.
